utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is the Case Number IT-03-68, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, and also good afternoon to my learned friends of the Defence. For the sake of the transcript, my name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution, and I'm here together with co-counsel, Mrs. Patricia Sellers, Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio, and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric, also for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I am Vasvija Vidovic. Together with Mr. John Jones I appear for the Defence of Mr. Naser Oric. With us is Ms. Adisa Mehic, our legal assistant, and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good afternoon to you and your team. Any preliminaries before we touch on ours? No. You -- we are expecting from you, Mr. Jones, a reply on two matters related to the forensic examination motion -- documents motion. One is what kind of lighting is envisaged or is anticipated to be used by your expert, and the other one is an estimate of when he expects to be able to hand to you his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't really care much when he finishes his forensic tests, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- I am much interested in knowing when he will hand you the report so you can then transmit the or file it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, indeed, Your Honour. Well, firstly on the first question, spectrometry will be used by the expert and my inclination is that he will use standard instrumental and visual methods of examination that will not affect the documents in any way, including infrared and ultraviolet lights and he'll also perform photography. That's the information I have. I did notice, Your Honour, just for what it's worth that the Prosecution expert also in their report used infrared luminescence examination and ultraviolet luminescence characteristics, that's from the -- the method set out in the report of their expert, ERN reference 03523858 [Realtime transcript read in error "03523538"]. So I take it there'll be no objection to those same techniques being used. Secondly, the indications are that once the experts receive the documents, there are 35 documents which he'll be examining, that he'll need at least two weeks to examine them and to prepare his report. If you give me a moment, Your Honour, I'll just consult my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I just add something. He will require two weeks to examine the documents and then an additional two weeks to write his report. So that is a total of one month. At any rate, he'll keep the documents for two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. That's what we needed to -- rather than speaking of one month, we're speaking of four weeks because, to be honest with you, every day counts in these circumstances, especially if it comes to a point where we will need to appoint our own expert. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just a reference to the ERN, it's wrongly recorded, it's 03523858 just for the record. That's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio, do you wish to add anything on your part? MR. DI FAZIO: I'm just saying that we've -- just now I was asking that -- arranging matters to get instructions on what Mr. Jones has just raised so that we can give our -- what I expect to be our final agreement tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. Tomorrow? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, if you can give it today I think it will be better because we can hand down our decision today, if that is the case. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I take it -- I mean, it's just a suggestion and I'm -- MR. DI FAZIO: Well, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- that if it's being suggested to you that the tests that are going -- the methodology and tests that is going to be adopted in this case is practically the same test that your expert -- MR. DI FAZIO: Then there should be no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then there should be no problem. But, please, I understand you have to take -- MR. DI FAZIO: I just want to cover ourselves, Your Honour, that's all. I expect there will be no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Last thing I would do is deprive you from that opportunity. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But please try and do that at the earliest. I don't think it should -- MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I've told people to make sure we can give you an answer by tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's perfect. If you can give it earlier, it would be appreciated. So, Mr. Dedic -- Madam, can you please bring him in? Today we are sitting to the same schedule, if you agree, that we adopted yesterday and the day before, a schedule to finish at 6.15 or thereabouts. It could be a few minutes more depending on how much time we lose in the meantime between now and then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Dedic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope you had a good rest and that you are in a position to proceed with your examination-in-chief. And then hopefully tomorrow we'll start with the cross-examination. We'll try to do our best to finish you by the end of our sitting on Friday. Okay? Again, I'm just reminding you as a formality that you are testifying under oath, or rather pursuant to your solemn declaration. And secondly, that you -- it's being suggested to you to use the time that we have more -- are there problems with interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That you confine your answers to the questions that are put to you rather than volunteer more information than you are asked for. All right? Okay. Thank you. Please, take yourself comfortable and Ms. Vidovic with proceed with her examination-in-chief now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Vidovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Dedic.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will continue from where we broke off yesterday. Yesterday I started asking you about the organisation of defence in Cerska itself, that is, and my question to you is the following. Can you describe the organisation of the Defence in Cerska for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The defence of Cerska was organised locally only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please what you mean by that, locally.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were smaller or bigger armed units that rallied around their leaders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what the names of these groups were.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most often these groups were named after the villages they came from, where they had been established. For example, Cerani, Rogosani, Skugurcani [phoen], and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During 1992 did you call them the Territorial Defence or not?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in 1992 and not later. We always used the names that I referred to just now, depending on their origin, what villages they came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly that certain villages had their own local leaders and their local armed groups?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it happen from time to time or not that in a single village there would be, say, two groups?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know very well the example of the village of Kokurtovici [phoen] which had two local groups that had rallied around two local leaders. Often they had poor cooperation or no cooperation whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe to the Trial Chamber what this cooperation was like in 1992 in general terms between these groups in Cerska, including Skugrici.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The cooperation between these groups in 1992 and 1993 was always on a voluntary basis only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, if somebody wanted to help someone, that's what they did. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, can you tell the Trial Chamber what the role of Ferid Hodzic was?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ferid Hodzic came from Vlasenica to Cerska at the end of May or beginning of June. He tried to unite the local groups that we referred to a few moments ago that were active in the villages and hamlets in the area of Cerska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say he came to Cerska at the May or beginning of June, were you referring to 1992 or --

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, did he manage in this effort to unite the local groups or not?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It failed. It was just an attempt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, did Ferid Hodzic have anything to offer to people so that they would be interested in listening to him at all? Were there any logistics in Cerska?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no logistics in Cerska and he had nothing to offer in that respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any barracks in the area of Cerska?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the area of Cerska before the war and during the war, there were no barracks whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any uniforms?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have any uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to the Trial Chamber the role of Semso Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Semso Salihovic was a brave man. He worked in the bauxite mine in Milici before the war, and he had around him a group of armed young men from Cerska. Since he was a brave man, they listened to him and they stood by him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall Becir Mekanic, who you referred to before, coming to the area of Cerska at some point? And if so, when did this happen?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this very well. This was the summer of 1992. He came to the area of Cerska along with a small group of armed men who were with him before, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, can you tell us whether they got along, Semso Salihovic, Becir Mekanic, Semso Salihovic, did they work in concert, did they agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know there was quite a bit of disagreement among them. I think that they were in competition. They were vying for the top position in that situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you spend most of your time in 1992, in which area, in which part of Cerska?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992 I stayed in Skugrici and Cerska, and I remained there until the area fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an armed group in Skugrici?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Skugrici there was an armed group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who headed that group?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This group in Skugrici was headed by Mirsad Sulejmanovic, Skejo, that was his nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, do you remember how many armed men were in this group? Can you describe this to us, what it looked like in the beginning, in May 1992, and all the way up to the fall of Srebrenica -- or rather, the fall of Cerska, how all of this evolved.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This group of Mirsad Sulejmanovic, Skejo, in May and June of 1992, I remember very well, had a total of 30 weapons available to them -- I'm sorry. Just before the area fell, that is to say in 1993, after some weapons had been seized or made at home, there was a total of 80 weapons that they had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, now we're only talking about the group of Mirsad Sulejmanovic, Skejo. This group that you belonged to, did it have any type of military command for itself?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. Not then, not later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the commander have assistant commanders, a deputy?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely -- almost all the groups that we mentioned were identical or similar. They had a leader, around whom they rallied, and no other organs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a particular post in this group?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had no particular position in this group except for the fact that I was its member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, during 1992 were you a member of the staff of the armed forces of Vlasenica during 1992?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of any such staff existing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After August 1992 or at any time until Cerska fell, were you assistant commander for morale?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was no one's assistant ever. I cannot even explain this to you what an assistant commander for morale is or does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you, in which area, during the course of 1992? Where did you spend most of your time, in which region?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the course of 1992, I spent most of my time with my group in Skugrici. When necessary, I went to other groups when we helped each other out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, according to what you know, after August 1992 was there some kind of staff or headquarters in Vlasenica that had its organ, for example, an assistant commander for morale that had its own staff units, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've never heard of any such staff and any kind of organs that you referred to just now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether Ferid Hodzic tried to organise something like that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm aware of his attempts, but I wish to repeat that that is what they were, attempts only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, in the course of 1992 in Cerska, did you have trained personnel or qualified personnel who could be staff members and make it possible for that staff to function from a military point of view?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no trained personnel. I think that I already mentioned once that in the entire area there was not a single professional military man. The leaders of these groups and the members of these groups for the most part were craftsmen, workers, factory workers, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, were you a reserve officer, you yourself?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I myself was a reserve officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe your actual line of work.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Atomic, biological, chemical warfare was my specialty and I was trained for the detection of radiological rays and chemical agents, and that's the only thing that I was trained for in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Prosecutor -- could the usher please show us Prosecution Exhibit P123. This is a document issued by the District Staff of the Tuzla defence dated the 29th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at the heading where it says "Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Tuzla district Defence Staff," and then it says: "Report on established staffs, institutions, and units of the armed forces." I will quote a part of the first paragraph which reads as follows, this is the third sentence: "In connection with item 2 of your order, we hereby inform you that we do not have the order to form units for any of the staff of the Supreme Command of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Mr. Dedic, from what I have just read, do you agree that it follows from this that this document was compiled in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you now please look at page 4 in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that's page 9 in English. The part that says "Vlasenica Defence Staff." Your Honour, I do apologise; it's 6 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 6 -- page 6, usher, not 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, please look at the subtitle "Vlasenica municipal Defence Staff." Look at items 4, 5, and 6, first of all. It says: "Vlasenica TO detachment, Cerska TO detachment, and the Djile TO attachment." And then look at these numbers 439, 439, 439, referring to the number of members, and then look at 1st Kladanj TO Company, 2nd Kladanj TO Company, and under 9, Pobudje TO Company. Please, can you comment on this document, this part of the document, that is?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What it says here under point 4, Vlasenica TO detachment, in my view might refer to a group from Vlasenica led by Mr. Hodzic. Under number 5 where it says Cerska TO detachment I think it refers to the group of Mr. Semso Salihovic. And under point 6, Djile TO detachment, I think this refers to the group led by Mr. Mekanic. The 1st Kladanj TO Company, however, and the 2nd Kladanj Company, I don't know what this might refer to because Kladanj was about 80 kilometres away from Vlasenica and we had no connection whatsoever with Kladanj. So I fail to understand why this is listed here. Under 9 it says "Pobudje TO Company." I mentioned Pobudje yesterday. There were armed groups there, but before the war and after the war, Pobudje was part of Bratunac municipality and had nothing to do with Vlasenica municipality. For this reason, I find this document odd and strange. I think it's unreliable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the field in Cerska, did you use the phrase "Territorial Defence"? I'm asking you about this because it's in the document.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish to repeat. We never used such titles on the ground. The names of the groups were exclusively linked to their places where they operated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you the following now: During summer and autumn of 1992, the groups that you have just described, your groups, were they part of the Srebrenica armed forces?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The groups I mentioned and described were never, either then or later on, until the fall of these areas, part of any group from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with respect to your armed groups, were they part of the Konjevic Polje groups?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you help the people from Konjevic Polje sometimes or did they help you?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was assistance on both sides, but I wish to repeat these instances of assistance were always and exclusively voluntary. There was no order that we had to provide assistance to one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of a man called Nurif Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell Their Honours who he was?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was a man who, in early August 1992, I think this was on the 4th of August but I can't be a hundred per cent certain of the day, arrived in Konjevic Polje from Tuzla. With him there arrived a group of uniformed and armed men and, as I learned later, there were about 400 of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard of the name of this group of men which arrived with him then? Was it a kind of Muslim brigade or not?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear it. I heard that these were men from the 16th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally have any contact with Nurif Rizvanovic ever?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had contacts with him on two occasions personally. The first time was in September 1992 and the second time in the same year but in early October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember your first contact with him? Can you describe this to Their Honours?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Rizvanovic from Konjevic Polje arrived in Cerska to see Mr. Ferid Hodzic. After that, Mr. Hodzic summoned a certain number of leaders of local groups and eminent people to a meeting in Cerska. At this meeting, Mr. Rizvanovic introduced himself as the commander of some Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. sort of Drina division, and he kept repeating to us that he had been sent by some sort of command from Tuzla to form this division and that he was its commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally attend this meeting?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, did he explain on that occasion what area the Drina division was supposed to cover?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He said that this division was supposed to cover the areas of Zvornik, Vlasenica, Bratunac, and Srebrenica municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say whether he had a plan?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He mentioned this plan of his and the main focus of that plan was that all these areas should be united, all the groups in those areas should be brought together and the Drina division should comprise all these groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now please show a document to the witness. This is document -- a document issued by the defence administration of the Tuzla canton. The title is "The Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Command of the Drina Division." The document was signed by the commander of the Drina Division, Nurif Rizvanovic and it's addressed to the attention of Mr. Ahmic. I will quote part of it. It says here: "Pursuant to decision number 1-7/92 of the 5th of September 1992, I was appointed commander of the Drina Division for the municipalities of Bratunac, Zvornik, Vlasenica, and Srebrenica. In view of this I would like to ask you to help me implement the following decisions. A stamp should be made" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment because it's before she what you said, Ms. Vidovic, I am sorry to interrupt you, but I think that this is important. What you said was interpreted to us "to help me implement the following decisions." What I have in the document or in the translation of the document that you are seeking to tender says: "To help me implement this decision." There is a slight difference, but I want to know exactly what you said because I suppose you're reading, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is an official translation, but I will read again precisely what it says in the original. It says: "In view of this, I ask you to make it possible for me to implement these decisions," in the plural.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1 is: "Mass media should keep repeating the order of the 9th of September, 1992, strictly confidential," I don't have to read every detail. Under 2: "A stamp should be made in accordance with the decision and sent to me by courier. 3: "I hereby authorise Sead Djozic to open giro account on behalf of the command. Itemise this for individual brigades from the decision. And then, for example, under 8: "I request to be given concrete decisions by the command of the armed forces in Tuzla for the further work of the division command in the free territory between Snagovo and Suceska and Luka." Mr. Dedic, first of all, do you know who Mr. Ahmic is.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Edhem Ahmic was the commander of some kind of groups from Bratunac in Tuzla. He wasn't in Cerska, Konjevic Polje, or Skugrici in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleague has drawn attention -- my attention to the fact that under 8 I request to be given concrete decisions in Tuzla for further work of the division command in the free territory from Snagovo to Suceska and Luka -- Suceska and Luka are both mentioned in the original --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I apologise to you, Mr. Dedic, you have explained who Mr. Ahmic was and I will ask you the following now. What it says in the document, this document that is, "I have been appointed commander of the Drina Division," does it correspond to what you were told by Nurif Rizvanovic when he arrived in Cerska in 1992?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, at that time in Cerska did he behave like someone who had been authorised by a higher command to issue orders to you on the ground?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely how he behaved. In my contacts with him, that was always the feeling I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you see him again? What was the next time you met Nurif Rizvanovic, could you describe it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My second contact with Mr. Rizvanovic was in early October 1992 in Skugrici. On that occasion he was visiting all the groups in the Skugrici and Cerska areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you then?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On that occasion he observed how we had dug the trenches, how we had made the lines, and he yelled at us. He told us it was no good, and he gave us instructions as to how we should do this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you from Skugrici discuss this with Ferid Hodzic and other people from Cerska, especially Ferid Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. I and we talked to him and others, and we learned later on that he had visited most of the groups in this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before I move on to the next question, could we have an exhibit number for this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What's the next number, please? D8 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D822, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So this document which consists of two pages in handwritten format without an ERN number in Serbo-Croat and a corresponding translation into English on one page is being tendered, received, and entered into the records as Defence Exhibit D822. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record we object to this document regarding the authentication. We notice that it is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can do that when the witness is not present. All right. I mean, just --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Make a mental note of it and then you object to it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic, I'm sorry for the interruption.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I explained the source of the document very clearly for the record and I believe that the Prosecutor has the same document in their archives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's avoid discussion on this in the presence of the witness, please, both of you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the usher could give the witness document 01837567. This is a document issued by the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, BH Armed Forces, combined Bratunac-Vlasenica-Zvornik units command, and the date is the 26th of October, 1992. The title of the document is "Combat Order."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I will read the whole document to you. "Having assessed the political and security situation in the free territory of Bratunac, Vlasenica, and Zvornik municipalities, I have decided to attack Grobic on the night of 27th to 28th October and return it to the hands of the BH Armed Forces. Company commanders will introduce the units of the attack from the rear by the way they know, after which the soldiers will deploy for small arms combat and return to Grobic. Commanders Semso, Becir, and Ferid are to take all necessary steps for units to mount a general attack from the rear at 0700 hours in the morning. According to this order, no soldier who was mobilised by the general instrument of the 23rd of June may refuse. Anyone doing so will be shot. "Signed, Commander Nurif Rizvanovic." I will ask you once again, when did Nurif arrive in your area, and when he arrived did he behave as a commander issuing orders when visiting your group, for instance?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He always behaved like a commander, as the leader of all the groups who had been active before his arrival. I often heard the group leaders saying that he was issuing orders to everyone he had contact with, acting like a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because he hasn't answered specifically, once you've ask the question again, when did Nurif Rizvanovic arrive in your area. When was it that he showed up in your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand whether the question was when did he arrive in the area or when did he arrive in Skugrici, where I spent most of my time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was -- well, you first described how Nurif Rizvanovic arrived in Konjevic Polje in early August. You said the 4th of August. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you described your first meeting with him in September 1992. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your second meeting with him, when did it take place?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In early October in Skugrici. He arrived according to the plan he kept talking about to tour the groups active in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And my question, Your Honour, I don't know how it was interpreted was:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he came to visit you in early October 1992, did he behave like a commander and issue orders or not?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer to this question is: Yes, he acted like a commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours, if this document can be given on exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This document which consists of two pages, one in Serbo-Croat with ERN 01837567 and the other one in -- corresponding translation into English thereafter is being tendered, received, and marked as Defence Exhibit D823.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now show the witness document P232, P232. This document is entitled "report by the commander of the Vlasenica armed forces on the combat readiness of these armed forces." And the number is 010828342 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you please look at the beginning of the document where it says: "From the beginning of the war in the area of organising the units of the armed forces," it's a little illegible, "of Bosnia and Herzegovina, we applied on several occasions to the competent staffs from this part of the free territory, but the Tuzla District Staff of the armed forces failed to find a way to cooperate so that five months into the war a unified security and information service and RIK have not been activated." Can you explain to Their Honours what RIK means.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is a unified system of control and command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you turn to page 2 of this document, please, and where it says "conclusions," there are several bullet points. And the third of these from the top says: "I hereby protest and do not accept the coerced appointment of Nurif Rizvanovic of the Drina Division because it does not reflect the situation." And this is signed by the Vlasenica OS commander, Ferid Hodzic. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with this I wish to ask you the following. Did the local group leaders whom you referred to accept Nurif Rizvanovic as their commander? Did they ever accept him as their commander, if you know?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, certainly, never, because they thought he was imposed from the outside. The local leaders, until his arrival, had had lots of problems to deal with and had dealt with them without him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your estimation, did the arrival of Nurif Rizvanovic worsen the situation as far as the local leaders in Konjevic Polje and Cerska were concerned or not?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, after his arrival and after his touring of certain groups, the situation grew worse. There was confusion because he was imposing himself as the main leader of all the existing groups in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One more question about this document. What it says here in this document, does it -- does it confirm Ferid Hodzic's attitude to Nurif Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, can you, usher, put, please, the original -- or the B/C/S version on the ELMO. The last page where the signature is, please. Mr. Dedic, are you familiar with Mr. Ferid Hodzic's signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I see before me -- well, it's not very clear, so I couldn't say with certainty that it was his signature. His signature was similar to this, yes, but I cannot be absolutely certain it's his signature because it's not very clear here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And what do the words just above the name Ferid Hodzic and the signature mean, "komandant OS Vlasenica," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know and as I mentioned earlier, Mr. Hodzic was the leader of a group of men who arrived with him from Vlasenica and the settlements around Vlasenica. The other armed groups in the area did not accept him. His idea until -- throughout the time before the fall of these areas was to unify them, but let me repeat he never succeeded in this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I just asked you a very simple question that you didn't answer. What is the meaning of the words "komandant OS Vlasenica"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What it says here, if he signed this, he signed himself as the commander of the armed forces of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And are you familiar with that stamp, which seems to be of the municipality of Vlasenica? Do you recognise that stamp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see quite clearly what it says here. "Municipal." I can't see every word here. It does say "municipal staff," yes, "Vlasenica."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Thank you. Yes -- any further questions on this document, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then you can take it away, please, Ms. Usher, Madam Usher, and then we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, now I'm going to ask you something different. Do you remember whether the beginning of November 1992 there were attempts to link up the armed groups of Cerska, Konjevic Polje with those of -- and Kamenica with Srebrenica -- sorry. I just need to go back to something else that the Judge asked you about. The commander of the armed forces of Vlasenica. Did I understand you correctly that your explanation was that Ferid Hodzic headed the refugee groups that had come to Cerska from Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I am going to ask you this other question. At the beginning of November 1992, attempts were made -- or rather, were attempts made for the armed groups of Cerska, Konjevic Polje, and Kamenica to be linked up to the Srebrenica armed groups?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Such an attempt was made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what happened with this attempt and when?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that we from the area of Skugrici and the area of Cerska, at the beginning of November 1992 were invited to some meeting that was held at the elementary school in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, do you remember who went from Cerska to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember well. The leaders of some groups were there. Among them was Mr. Besir Aljukic, Mr. Saban Muminovic, Mr. Ferid Hodzic. I was there and some other prominent persons from Cerska and Skugrici were there and at this moment I cannot remember their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who you found there?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We came there during the night because it was always risky to go from Cerska to Konjevic Polje. We found a group of people from Konjevic Polje there. Among them I recognised Mr. Veiz Sabic, Mr. Dzemail Becirovic and Mr. Hamed Salihovic from Srebrenica --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether anyone else from Srebrenica was there with Mr. Hamed?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was sitting in the middle. Next to him were two men whom I do not know. They were from Srebrenica, they came from him. I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Hamed Salihovic from before?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Mr. Salihovic from before. He was a teacher, a geography teacher. I knew him from before the war, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Naser Oric was present during the meeting?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Oric was not at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Oric from before that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know Mr. Oric personally then or before the war either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, had you heard of Naser Oric before that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had heard of him during the war, that he was some very young man from Potocari who was fighting like a lion, like a dragon from Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of anyone else who was fighting in the area of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to Mr. Oric, in the area of Srebrenica in a village called Suceska, Zulfo Tursunovic was fighting. His nickname was Cica. He had around him a certain number of armed men who were resisting the enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you know that. Did you hear about that from someone?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that during the summer from Mr. Mekanic. He was in the area before he had to leave. He was near Suceska and he is the one who told me about this, that there was a very brave, old man there resisting the enemy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I will take you back to the meeting that you mentioned that you had come to. Do you remember whether Naser Oric was mentioned at that meeting at all?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, mentioned he was. Mr. Salihovic then gave some ideas to the effect that Mr. Oric could, according to Salihovic's idea, be commander of all the forces from Cerska, Kamenica, Konjevic Polje, and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who did most of the talking at that meeting, generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. At all meetings related to such matters it was Mr. Salihovic who did most of the talking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his idea then? Can you tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. His idea was that all armed forces -- or rather, armed groups from Skugrici, Cerska, Kamenica, Konjevic Polje, and Srebrenica should be brought together, placed under a single command, because in his opinion that was the only way to resist the enemy. Because this was a time of very intensive attacks by the Serb forces in this area. To be quite honest, I thought that this was a very good idea and a very reasonable idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the month of November, did you attend any other such meetings?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I attended two other meetings. We made a humongous effort in order to get to Konjevic Polje because the situation was worsening by the day. I think we managed to do that sometime by mid-November, but after that we no longer managed to meet up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember these two meetings that you attended, do you remember whether Oric was present?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no, or at least I did not see him where I was sitting. I never saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Hamed Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was always at all the meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, at these meetings were any decisions reached?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of decision?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A decision was made to set up a War Presidency of the subregion, and the president of this War Presidency would be Mr. Salihovic. And to establish a staff of the armed forces of the subregion that would be headed by Mr. Oric, as commander. And the Chief of Staff would be Mr. Ferid Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the witness an exhibit. It is P181. This is a decision of the War Presidency dated the 4th of November, 1992. It was reached in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that one of the meetings that you attended?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to quote part of this decision where it says: "The War Presidency of the subregion of the municipalities of Srebrenica, Bratunac, Vlasenica, and Zvornik at the session held in Konjevic Polje on the 4th of November, 1992, municipality of Bratunac, reached a decision on joining the armed forces of the municipalities of Srebrenica, Bratunac, Vlasenica, and Zvornik into the joined armed forces of the subregion of the municipalities of Srebrenica, Bratunac, Vlasenica, and Zvornik." And the next part: "The armed forces of the municipalities of Srebrenica, Bratunac, Vlasenica, Zvornik shall be subordinated to the staff of the armed forces of the subregion of the municipalities of Srebrenica, Bratunac, Vlasenica, and Zvornik." In connection with this I will ask you the following: Does this decision reflect what you said a few moments ago in terms of what had been decided to join up the armed forces in the area?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were certain people elected to particular positions then?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You explained that Hamed Salihovic was elected president of the War Presidency, Naser Oric and Ferid Hodzic to certain positions as well. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. So let us not repeat that. But I shall ask you the following. Were you given some assignment there?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was given an assignment to deal with certain administrative matters in the subregion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please, to the best of your knowledge, did Hamed Salihovic try as much as he could or did he not try to get this subregion working?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the witness another document now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Perhaps this answer is not clear enough. Please, my question was: To the best of your knowledge, did Hamed Salihovic try to do everything that was within his ability to get this subregion working and functioning?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My answer was yes. He worked on that. He wanted to get it working. I repeat that this was his idea and remained his idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at this document, please. This is a document of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Armed Forces of the free territory from the 6th of November, 1992. The Prosecution number is 02995666, and it is a document that was signed on the left-hand side by the president of the War Presidency of the subregion Hamed Salihovic and it says: "To Commanders Oric and Semso Salihovic." It says: "Order. "In order to resolve the -- resolve the Srebrenica-Cerska communication issues, you must provide accommodation and meals for (Halil Mehmedovic). In this way the planned communications would be ready and we would have a communications centre for Srebrenica. Together with the above-named person, Senahid Baibic whom you have sent to be trained shall work together with the above-mentioned person. It is necessary for you to have two or three persons who will charge the generator and be in charge of securing energy for the radio station. Persons who shall be professionally competent to carry out these tasks. The person we are sending has the professional expertise and has been trained to work since it would take too long to train this person. Any problems that occur shall be resolved by agreed communications." Now, in relation to this document I'm asking you the following: First and foremost, have you seen this document -- or rather, before I showed it to you?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Hamed Salihovic's signature?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, do you know whether Hamed Salihovic did everything he could for the communications service to start functioning between Srebrenica and Cerska?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He tried to get this communication working because before there were no communications between Cerska and Srebrenica. However, this communication was never established, not even later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You understand that we are talking about radio communications here?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, radio communications.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, do you know about any orders being issued by Hamed Salihovic to that effect?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know this name Senahid?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very -- I know it very well. He was a ham radio operator. He went there on Mr. Salihovic's orders. He was supposed to be trained there, but I repeat once again this communication was never established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may this document please be given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Vidovic. This document which consists of two pages, one in the Serbo-Croat language with ERN 02995666. And the other with a corresponding translation into English is being tendered, received, and marked as Defence Exhibit D824.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to this area I'm going to put another question to you. Did you talk to Mr. Semso Salihovic about Hamed Salihovic ever? In other words, do you know that Hamed tried to issue orders to Semso in this period?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Salihovic often said to me, That man is boring me to tears with all his orders. I remember those comments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the witness D267. This is a report of the subregion of the municipalities of Srebrenica, Vlasenica, Bratunac, and Zvornik, dated the 18th of November, 1992, sent to the Main Staff and to the public and it says "Subject: Report."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to quote some of this document to you. It says: "Facing the same problems and endangered by the same enemy, the armed forces of Srebrenica, Bratunac, Vlasenica, and Zvornik have joined ranks and placed themselves under one command. This is all because these areas have been endangered both by Serbia and by the extremist part of the SDS and are in -- are completely surrounded. Lately the aggressor has been building up his armoured mechanised units along the Drina river, particularly in Skelani and on the bridge across the Drina near Bratunac." And please, you can see down here it says: "President of the subregional War Presidency, Salihovic," and you can see it says here "received ham radio station, Sarajevo." In connection with this I shall ask you the following. You said to us a few moments ago that a decision had been passed to establish the subregion on the 4th of November 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at this document now dated the 18th of November, 1992, and it says there armed forces of Srebrenica, Bratunac, Vlasenica, and Zvornik have joined ranks and placed themselves under a single command. My question in relation to this is the following: Was this actually the case, these units, these forces, these groups, call them what you will, did they place themselves under a single command on the ground by the 18th of November, 1992, that is to say within those 12 days? All of these groups of Srebrenica, Bratunac, Vlasenica, and Zvornik. What is your comment in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish to note that the period when this document was written, namely the 18th of November, 1992, was a period of intensive Serb attacks at these areas. When communications were practically interrupted between Konjevic Polje, Cerska, and Skugrici. It is practically impossible, at least for me as a person who was a professional soldier, that somebody could within 14 days carry out this kind of assignment, joining up armed groups from four very distant municipalities, or rather four parts of municipalities because these were not the entire prewar municipalities. Over such a short period of time, in my opinion, that is impossible. It is undo-able. On the contrary, as far as I know the situation on the ground was far worse. People were even more separated from one another because of enemy activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly? In other words, are you saying that the content of this document is not correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The content of this document is absolutely incorrect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll ask you something else about this. You said that Ferid Hodzic was elected Chief of Staff of the armed forces of the subregion. In fact, to your knowledge did he ever start carrying out these duties of Chief of Staff of the armed forces of the subregion?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He never carried out these duties. He was carrying out the same tasks that he did from the moment he came to Cerska until its fall. He was there and he was never in the role of Chief of Staff of the subregion, as you said in your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, you said that you were given some assignments in terms of some administrative work for the staff. Did you ever do anything that had to do with the subregion, any kind of work?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as that particular work is concerned, I did not write a single word. May I just say one more thing? It's not that I wouldn't want to do that, but it was impossible. I repeat once again, this was a time of great difficulty and isolation for the area. So communication always involved casualties and loss of human life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're talking here about the 18th of November. Could you even get to the area of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From mid-November 1992, we were practically cut off from Konjevic Polje, too. From time to time, people who were either very brave or, if I may say so, totally crazy managed to get from one place to another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now play D72, please. This is part of the footage about the establishment of the Bratunac Brigade, the 14th of November, 1992. Could it please be played from 00.02.27 until the end. I think -- or rather, this is a video with subtitles. This is the speech of General Milenko Zivanovic, the commander of the Drina Corps, and you can see the translation there. Could you please play it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Here he is. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Dedic, did you hear General Zivanovic in this speech of his referring to the encircled 80.000 Turks of Podrinje? Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, do you agree that this word "the Turks" pertains to the Muslims of the area?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what they called us throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Serbs?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, did you notice the commander of the Drina Corps saying "the Turks of Cerska cannot join up with the Srebrenica Turks nor can the Kladanj Turks go to Cerska." This speech of his from November 1992, does it reflect the real situation regarding the encirclement of Cerska and the isolation of Cerska and Srebrenica on the ground?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you described the reasons for the impossibility of the subregion beginning to function, was the main reason for this impossibility the physical isolation between Srebrenica and Cerska, as mentioned in this video?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. The main reason was the total isolation of these areas; they were cut off from each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, to the way, the manner, the question is put to the witness. This is a form of guiding because so far the witness hasn't used the word "impossibilities" and "reasons for impossibility" and so forth. So at least it is a leading question, but also it's guiding the witness to a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're repeating what General Milenko Zivanovic stated in his speech, that these people could no longer reach or communicate with each other because they were encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I refer to the first part of the question, and I quote on line 30 -- no, page 35, line 14: "Question: When you described the reasons for the impossibility of the subregion beginning to function," those are not words that are used by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What had he stated before? What had he stated before? He was asked whether this subregion ever functioned, whether Ferid Hodzic ever functioned as Chief of Staff, whether this one ever functioned or that one ever functioned. He was very categoric.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: With all due respect, Your Honour, it's an impossibility --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond, Your Honour? In lines 25 and 26 in answer to my question, the witness said very clearly that it was not possible for the subregion to start functioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which lines of which page?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, actually our sequence is maybe slightly out because the answer was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I am less advanced than you are and my page arrived to line 25 on each page. It never goes to 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. In fact, as I say, the reference which we have here is -- in terms of page and line is not the best one. I think the time should be correct, 15.37 ... In any event, the answer is, when he was asked whether he did any of that kind of work. He said: "No, as far as that particular work is concerned, I did not write single word. May I just say one more thing? It's not that I wouldn't want to do that, but it was impossible. I repeat again this was a time of great difficulty and isolation of the area, so communication always involved casualties and loss of human life." So he did mention an impossibility, at least for him, to perform these functions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, I think we are wasting time. Do you insist on your objection, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let's clarify this once again. Please, in mid-November 1992, was it possible for any communication to take place between Srebrenica and Cerska? And is the description provided by General Zivanovic correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The description of the situation provided by General Zivanovic is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under such conditions, to the best of your knowledge, was it possible for the subregion to function?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You described for us the situation of physical isolation and separation in this area. Do you know of any cases where some people did manage get through to Cerska from other areas?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were such instances, but I know of only two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what would happen for the most part with people trying to go from Cerska toward Kladanj, for example, or from Cerska toward Konjevic Polje and Srebrenica? What would happen to those people?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately most such people never arrived at their destination, and their fate remains unknown to this day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you knew of two instances where people managed to pass through. Can you explain this to Their Honours?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A young man, whose nickname was Jastreb set out from Cerska to Srebrenica. While I was in Cerska, he did not return. When Cerska fell and I arrived in Srebrenica, I thought I would find him there. But several months later I learned that he had again set out to Cerska but never arrived there. Another case I know of is that of Mr. Kadir Hamidovic, who sometime before Christmas 1993 arrived from Glogova to Skugrici. He arrived alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll come back to him, but let me ask you another question pertaining to the subregion. After the fall of Cerska and your arrival in Srebrenica, did you personally have occasion to talk to Hamed Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke to Mr. Hamed Salihovic and he told me that throughout that time he had been trying by way of Tuzla or Sarajevo to get some kind of assistance for the people of Cerska and Konjevic Polje. He was not, however, successful in this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he threatened the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina with secession?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the end he told me that he had even tried to get people to understand the seriousness of the situation by saying that, but he was not successful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I'll move on to another topic now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher please show the witness document P213, P213. The document is entitled "Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Srebrenica armed forces staff." The date is the 13th of February, 1993, and the document reads as follows: "Pursuant to the decree law issued by the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina on general mobilisation and pursuant to the decision of the War Presidency of the subregion on the general mobilisation of conscripts from Srebrenica, Bratunac, Vlasenica, and Zvornik municipalities, as well as with the consent of the chief of the Main Staff of the Bosnia-Herzegovina army, Sefer Halilovic, I hereby order: "All conscripts from the areas of Srebrenica, Bratunac, and Vlasenica municipalities who are subject to military service and who are at the front in the BH Army 2nd Corps area of responsibility shall come immediately to the free territory of the subregion with their weapons. "All organised units from the area of the above-mentioned municipalities are to be informed about this already, namely the following: Ahmet Duric, Latif Zalfalori, and others." And this is allegedly signed by the Srebrenica armed forces commander, Naser Oric. First of all, I will ask you the following. In Cerska did you hear of any order issued by the subregion War Presidency on general mobilisation in February 1993?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. February 1993 was a period when no one could leave the area in any direction. The whole area was pockmarked with shell holes, and it would have been incredible for someone to bring such a document there without getting killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of 1992, 1993, 1994, did you ever hear of the existence of a decree law issued by the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, either in Cerska or Srebrenica, up to 1995?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never heard of such a decree and, to be quite honest, the first time in my life I heard of a decree law was in 2004 when I retired under such a law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of the existence of a decree law from anyone in Srebrenica in 1992, 3, or 4?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never heard of such a thing. And in 1995 when I went over to the free territory, I never saw anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now look at this part of the document where it says that: "All conscripts from the areas of Srebrenica, Bratunac, and Vlasenica municipalities who are liable for military service and who are at the front in the area of responsibility of the BH army 2nd Corps should immediately come with their weapons to the free territory of the subregion." Please, according to what you know about the situation in the area, would this have been feasible?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By your leave, this order looks very odd to me. It's incredible. For somebody from Srebrenica to issue orders to soldiers in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Corps, that's one point; and another point is that they should come immediately I travelled from Srebrenica to Tuzla for eight days and eight nights. I don't know if that means immediately. To me, in my view, "immediately" means something different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of Ahmet Duric and Latif Zalfalori as some kind of important people to whom such an order should be conveyed?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard of either of these. And Zalfalori, as it says in this document, I've never heard of such a name. This looks like Greek to me. I never heard of anyone with such a name in the area where I lived, Zalfalori.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And on the basis of what you have seen, can you accept this document as correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's have a half an hour break starting from now. That means we will reconvene at 4.30. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So -- MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, he's got good news. Mr. Di Fazio is -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Good news. Yes, there's no problem. We can go ahead with those tests to be conducted. I suggest that the case manager from the Defence contact our case manager and we're in the process of arranging the protocol or documentation that we intend to create to trace the documents from here, from our possession --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. MR. DI FAZIO: -- to Sarajevo and back again and we'll get that material ready and it can now go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just a moment. Perhaps you could copy and paste this straight away and send it to Wade. The other thing is, just to prepare you more or less for what the decision will provide. The decision will provide first and foremost that the registrar must communicate to us and to both of you the name of the special representative that will actually be the one appointed to be in charge of collecting the documents from your custody and handing them over to the expert which will be -- who will be mentioned in the order itself. Okay? Secondly, there will be nothing in the order itself authorising your expert to do anything, because that's your responsibility. We are not appointing him, you are appointing him. Thirdly, the -- that before delivery is affected, your expert will need to identify himself, in other words the special representative must be satisfied of the identity of the person who will receive these documents, that is being the same person that is being appointed by you. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. And then when delivery is affected, is completed, then the special representative of the registry will communicate to us the date and time so that the month that we will be establishing for the completion of this exercise will start running from that day. This is basically in essence, et cetera, we were waiting for your information and now this needs to be included in the draft that I handed to Mr. Pittman earlier on during the break. Because, as you know, when we say we'll have a half an hour's break, we usually don't include ourselves. And we end up doing work as well. So let's continue with Mr. Dedic. Do you think you will finish with him today or not, Ms. Vidovic? I'm not calling upon you to finish with him today, but it's just a question of trying to find out whether he can anticipate to go home on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it might be possible to finish today, but if I don't I will take only a brief time tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's perfect. So let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Dedic, I will go back to the events of Christmas 1993. In your testimony you said that just before Christmas Kadir Hamidovic arrived in Cerska from Glogova. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any contact with you personally? Did you personally have contact with him?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have personal contact with him because Mr. Hamidovic has a sister who is married in Skugrici, and he would occasionally come to visit her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, what exactly did he say to you when he arrived on the 7th of January in Cerska, before the 7th of January that is?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he arrived before the 7th of January. And he told me that the population of Glogova was taking refuge in Glogova Mountain, that they were exposed to the cold. Quite a few of them had no footwear and no food, and that they were living in very difficult conditions. He also said that a group of people from the village of Glogova were in the village of Cizmici where the leader of the group was, Mr. Ejub Golic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you about any fighting in late December 1992?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he did. The inhabitants of Glogova who had been cut off from each other were trying to link up again. And thanks to Mr. Golic and the armed men with him, he managed to break through some Serb lines and link up with the population of Glogova which was in the area of Glogova and Glogova Mountain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not he mentioned any Serb units of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He said that there were numerous forces in Kravica, that apart from the local population of Kravica, there were also policemen from Bijeljina, some units from the Krajina, and he even mentioned the name of a certain Mauzer as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether he arrived only to visit his sister or whether he brought some kind of message from Ejub Golic to somebody?

utterances.speaker: EJUB DEDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to what he said I think that he only visited his sister by the way, and that in fact he had come to ask for assistance for the people whom I have just mentioned who were living in very difficult conditions. And he also mentioned that Mr. Golic had sent people to other places to ask for assistance because the inhabitants of Glogova were surrounded, exposed to attacks and shelling, and the attacks were especially fierce from Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
